Definition: from a compound of G5204 and a derivative of G3700 (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical":--have the dropsy.
BiblicalUsage: The word hydrōpikós carries the sense of to suffer from dropsy. In Luke 14:2, the text says "there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy."
TheologicalSignificance: I read hydrōpikós plainly — it means to suffer from dropsy, and I do not build a doctrine on it.
